name: Rhodogune of Parthia
summary:
Rhodogune of Parthia was a queen of the Seleucid Empire by marriage to Demetrius II Nicator. She was born into the royal family of Parthia and became a powerful figure in the ancient world.

 Born around 130 BCE, Rhodogune married Demetrius II in 113 BCE and played an important role in his reign as co-ruler. As the daughter of the Parthian king Mithridates I, she was also sister to Phraates II, who would eventually succeed her brother as king.

 After Demetrius II's death in 83 BCE, Rhodogune became a prominent figure in the Seleucid Empire's politics, often acting as regent for her nephew Antiochus VIII.

 Her legacy extends to the art and architecture of the time, with several sculptures and coins bearing her likeness. Despite her influence, not much is known about her personal life or motivations beyond her strategic marriages and royal connections.

 Rhodogune's story highlights the intricate web of alliances and power struggles in the ancient world, showcasing the complex nature of imperial politics during this period.
